title: Crises source added only to check_reject_balance — the new eras rows may still pass vacuously via check_reject_eras
evidence:
crises       = transmute([]u8)string(CRISES_VALID), // Perkins r3 B1: WITHOUT the crises source the loader dies in crises.json BEFORE balance, and every row "passes" through the non-balance trivial branch - the whole table was vacuous
...
+        {"box piece before its era", replace1(`{"eras": [` + ERAS_ROW + `]}`, `"router_basic": 6`, `"router_mid": 6`, 1), "dead stock before its era"},
+        {"box spool dead stock", replace1(`{"eras": [` + ERAS_ROW + `]}`, `"fiber": 0}`, `"fiber": 5}`, 1), "dead stock — shift the cap"},
     }
     for r in eras_rows {
         check_reject_eras(t, r.doc, r.rule)
detail: Per the B1 comment the loader parses crises.json before balance and therefore before eras; the diff fixes only check_reject_balance, never check_reject_eras, so the two new dead-stock rows can trivially pass through the same non-eras branch this diff calls a bug.
recommended_fix: Add crises = transmute([]u8)string(CRISES_VALID) to check_reject_eras (and any other per-file check helper) and verify a row actually reaches the eras parser.

title: dots_during_crisis gate can false-fail: latch set after the event loop excludes trigger-tick dots and short crisis windows
detail: saw_crisis_active latches only after each tick's event loop, so a dot on the trigger tick never counts; a crisis window shorter than dot_interval (up to 20000 ticks per the new catalog ceiling) yields zero counted dots and a harness FAIL with nothing actually broken.
recommended_fix: Count on len(s.crisis.active) > 0 alone (drop the latch conjunct) and gate the FAIL on the crisis window actually overlapping a due dot.

title: crises_resolved counter has no consumer anywhere in the diff
evidence:
+    crises_resolved: i32, // internal: Crisis_Resolved events seen
...
+            if e.tag == pp.EVENT_TAG_CRISIS_RESOLVED do stats.crises_resolved += 1
detail: The new field is incremented but never read — the econ_check hunk only consumes crises and dots_during_crisis. Dead instrumentation, or a missing triggered==resolved assertion.
recommended_fix: Consume it (e.g. fail when crises_resolved != crises) or delete the field and its increment.

title: Post-crisis recovery property deleted, not redirected — nothing now asserts dots land after a crisis resolves
evidence:
-    dots_post_crisis: i32, // dots AFTER the last crisis resolved (the no-death-spiral recovery)
...
-        if stats.crises >= 1 && stats.dots_post_crisis == 0 {
-            fmt.println("  FAIL: no dot landed after the crisis — the death spiral the floor must absorb")
+    dots_during_crisis: i32, // dots while a crisis was ACTIVE (the floor spoke under crisis - the Q7 no-death-spiral half the SIM owns)
detail: The old check verified recovery after the crisis; the new one verifies activity during it. The renamed comment still claims the 'no-death-spiral half', but that property is no longer asserted anywhere shown — a coverage regression dressed as a rename.
recommended_fix: Keep a post-crisis dot counter alongside dots_during_crisis, or cite where the recovery property is now owned.

title: _comment replaced with a truncated sentence and unbalanced parenthesis
evidence:

+   "_comment": "... Eras 1/2 are UNCHANGED (dormant in the MVP — the shipped app starts at Foundations (era 1, USER RULING 2026-08-28) and advances via the 6.2 gate",
detail: The replacement stops mid-thought ('and advances via the 6.2 gate') and never closes the '(dormant in the MVP' parenthesis — a malformed edit in the only changed line of the file.
recommended_fix: Complete the sentence (advance-gate mechanics, era re-tune ownership) and balance the parentheses.

title: testing_lvl_ok guard silently skips the (d)+(e) routed-halo invariant on a broken fixture
detail: Skip is not fail: nothing in this hunk records a failure when testing_lvl_ok is false, so the ONE-look halo/width pin can go entirely unverified while the harness reports clean.
recommended_fix: Emit an explicit FAIL (or precondition assert) when testing_lvl_ok is false instead of quietly bypassing the leg.

title: st.box_enabled set true before box_enable — ordering may defeat an idempotence guard
detail: If box_enable early-returns when already enabled, the pre-set flag skips initialization; if it does not, the manual set is redundant. Either way the ordering is load-bearing and uncommented, unlike every neighboring line.
recommended_fix: Let box_enable own the flag (drop the pre-set), or comment why the flag must be true before the call.

title: Test pins a 'no decimals' message for an integer-overflow input
evidence: +        {"box interval over i32 (the strict-int overflow path)", replace1(BAL_VALID, `"dot_interval_ticks": 2400`, `"dot_interval_ticks": 1099511627776`, 1), "clock keys must be integers (no decimals)"},
detail: 1099511627776 is a valid integer; the row now actively pins a 'no decimals' diagnostic to the out-of-i32 path, teaching the loader to misreport range overflow as a formatting problem.
recommended_fix: Give the strict-int overflow path its own message naming the acceptable range, and pin that instead.

title: Fixture-wide kit grant touches every pullback_test_app consumer; no sibling expectations updated in the diff
